quick_summaries.title_en: Dr. Grasp-RL: Diverse and Robust Dexterous Grasping via Reinforcement Learning
quick_summaries.title_zh: Dr. Grasp-RL：基于时间反转课程强化学习的多样化鲁棒灵巧抓取
quick_summaries.abstract: Human interaction with physical objects relies on a combination of dexterity and robustness. In robotic manipulation, dexterity requires not only flexible end effectors but also a diverse repertoire of manipulation strategies, while robustness requires closed-loop adaptation to disturbances and unexpected situations. Two prominent research directions in dexterous grasping have largely addressed these capabilities separately. Generative approaches model multimodal distributions to produce diverse grasp poses, but their reliance on open-loop execution can limit robustness. Reinforcement learning approaches learn closed-loop grasping policies, but can converge to a narrow range of successful grasping strategies, limiting behavioral diversity. We introduce a time-reversed curriculum with a coordinated reset mechanism that enables a simple MLP policy trained with PPO to capture multiple modes of the grasp-pose distribution while maintaining closed-loop control. Experiments demonstrate both diverse grasping behaviors and robust closed-loop execution. Trained on only approximately 400 objects, our policy further demonstrates strong generalization when evaluated on more than 20,000 unseen objects.
quick_summaries.reason: 通过时间反转课程与协同重置机制让简单 MLP-PPO 策略学会多模态灵巧抓握姿态并维持闭环抗扰能力，仅在约 400 个物体上训练即泛化至超 20,000 个未见物体。

quick_summaries.title_en: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
quick_summaries.title_zh: DexDuet：从单次人类示教学习保持接触关系的双臂灵巧操作
quick_summaries.abstract: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present DexDuet, a framework that learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from a single human demonstration. DexDuet employs two interaction rewards to preserve human hand-object configurations and contacts. To enable coordinated manipulation, we factorize the bimanual policy into two weight-sharing per-hand policies that condition on each other's states. We further propose assisted reference-state initialization (A-RSI), an adaptive curriculum that adjusts object assistance and training starts across demonstration segments to overcome difficult manipulation phases. Across four benchmarks spanning three simulators and five robot embodiments, DexDuet improves object-tracking ADD-AUC by 11 to 41 points over the corresponding baselines while consistently achieving better contact preservation. Notably, among 122 paired runs with comparable object-tracking accuracy, DexDuet preserves the human's contacts better in 117 cases. Code and videos are available at this https URL

quick_summaries.title_en: Force2Act: A Force-Aware Visuomotor Policy for Generalizable Compliant Robot Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: Force2Act：面向可泛化柔顺机器人操作的力感知视觉运动策略
quick_summaries.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to regulate the force it applies, not only where it moves. quick_summaries.title_en: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation

quick_summaries.title_en: VTLA-RL: Learning Visuotactile Policies for Load-Adaptive Grasping
quick_summaries.title_zh: VTLA-RL：面向负载自适应抓取的视觉-触觉语言动作强化学习后训练

quick_summaries.title_en: Distilling Touch into Vision-Only Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation

quick_summaries.title_en: DUO Policy: Bridging Human Video Coverage and Robot Precision for Fine-Grained Manipulation

quick_summaries.title_en: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: WeaveVLA：面向视觉-语言-动作模型的 3D 关系接地

quick_summaries.title_en: SparQ4D: Learning to Act through Sparse 4D Queries
quick_summaries.title_zh: SparQ4D：通过稀疏 4D 查询学习机器人操作策略
quick_summaries.abstract: Successful manipulation requires a policy to understand where things are and how they will move, yet action demonstrations leave this spatiotemporal structure implicit. At its core is a query-based decoder attached to a pretrained policy, which casts many spatialtemporal tasks into one unified interface (e.g. depth, 2D/3D point motion, multi-view correspondence, and hand-eye relations). quick_summaries.title_en: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models

quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. quick_summaries.title_en: Wrist-Camera Video Diffusion as Generalizable Robot Policies
quick_summaries.title_zh: WVP：以腕部相机视频扩散作为跨具身可泛化机器人策略
quick_summaries.abstract: A generalist manipulation policy should perform new tasks, operate in unfamiliar scenes, and transfer skills across robot embodiments. Model stitching maps the generator's predicted latents directly into the estimator's intermediate feature space, bypassing RGB decoding. This decomposition allows task knowledge to expand through broad human and robot video data while reusing geometric motion estimation across tasks and embodiments. The resulting pose estimator transfers across Franka Panda, PiPER-X, and Galaxea R1 Pro without further fine-tuning. Across tabletop and laundry-room settings, WVP generalizes to tasks ranging from precise grasping and inserting to handling deformable objects, achieving a success rate of over 50% in zero-shot out-of-distribution evaluations. quick_summaries.title_en: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine

quick_summaries.abstract: Flow-matching policies integrate a velocity field from a fixed, observation-independent Gaussian source. quick_summaries.title_en: Spiking World-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: SpikingWAM：面向机器人操作的脉冲神经网络世界-动作模型

quick_summaries.title_en: Detecting Is Not Choosing: What a World Model Needs to Keep a VLA Policy Safe
quick_summaries.title_zh: 检测不等于择优：探究世界模型守护 VLA 策略安全的真正需求
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies complete most benchmark tasks but often violate safety constraints. Since they are stochastic, one remedy is to sample several candidate action chunks and execute one that a world model predicts is safe. We ask what such a model must do. In simulation, a lookahead safety filter with the simulator as an exact world model raises the safety rate of three VLA policies on LIBERO and of pi0.5 on LIBERO-Plus by 11.5 to 25.7 points. It also helps pi0.5 on three RoboCasa tasks. Learned critics trained on one policy's data detect dangerous states (pooled AUROC up to 0.864) but rank candidates at one state close to chance (within-decision AUROC 0.551-0.560), and the learned dynamics and video models we test do no better. When the simulator's state is perturbed, selection degrades long before detection. In the loop, a median position error of 3.18 mm removes 70% of the gain on LIBERO-Spatial, partly because the error also corrupts the displacement check. On LIBERO-10 the loss is smaller, and the intervals overlap. The median does not predict the cost: a pixel reader with a 0.56 mm median error keeps 6.5 points less of the gain than Gaussian error of a similar median. A world model for safety should thus be judged by within-state ranking, and its state must be accurate in the tail and on handled objects, not only in the median.

quick_summaries.title_en: RoboLiveMem: Is Robot Memory Solved When the World Does Not Wait?
quick_summaries.title_zh: RoboLiveMem：当物理世界不等待思考时，机器人记忆是否已解决？
quick_summaries.abstract: Robot agents built on frontier vision-language models now solve most robot memory benchmarks. Does this mean they can remember what they need in a home, where people and machines keep moving things? Existing memory benchmarks cannot answer this question, because they pause the simulator while the model thinks: nothing can change during a decision, so whatever the robot remembers is still true when it acts. quick_summaries.title_en: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
quick_summaries.title_zh: TabAct：表格基础模型竟是高效的上下文机器人学习器
quick_summaries.abstract: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context. We introduce TabAct, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. The predictor receives no robot-specific training or target-task fine-tuning. With one target-task demonstration available to each method, TabAct with TabICLv2 achieves the highest average success among all evaluated methods on both LIBERO and Meta-World, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.9 and 5.8 percentage points, respectively. Additional demonstrations improve control without updating model weights: with five demonstrations, success reaches 94.2% on LIBERO-Object. These results demonstrate that generic numerical pretraining can provide an effective foundation for in-context robot learning.
quick_summaries.reason: 将视觉模仿转化为数值回归问题，用冻结视觉与本体特征及示教动作块作为上下文样本输入冻结表格基础模型 TabICLv2，单示教下在 LIBERO 与 Meta-World 分别超越最强基线 20.9 与 5.8 个百分点。

quick_summaries.title_en: Counterfactual Velocity Steering for World Action Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: 世界-动作模型的反事实速度场纠偏研究
quick_summaries.abstract: Flow-based robot policies generate actions by repeatedly evaluating a conditional velocity field, so test-time bias correction seems simple: query the action expert under a task-agnostic condition and subtract that velocity from the task-conditioned prediction. We show this is often wrong. On Fast-WAM across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, mean-instruction predictions align strongly with task-conditioned velocities (cosine approximately 0.94-0.95). Averaging eight completed-state references barely cancels this direction: their mean norm is 98.3% of the mean individual norm. References thus contain a large shared transport component, not only harmful bias, and aggressive subtraction damages generation. We propose a same-state diagnostic and shrinkage analysis showing that the optimal correction scale depends on reference signal-to-noise. This motivates geometry-calibrated action debiasing, which removes only the component orthogonal to the task velocity and predicts a small task-dependent scale from instruction geometry. In controlled RoboTwin experiments, corrupting instructions still permits 25.1% success (50 tasks, 20 episodes), whereas dynamic visual corruption nearly eliminates success. quick_summaries.title_en: Beyond Which: Where, How, and When in Vision-Language-Action Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: $\mathcal{W}^3\mathcal{H}$-VLA：统筹“是什么、在哪里、如何做与何时用”的 VLA 框架
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically rely on vision-language model (VLM) features as the primary perceptual source for action prediction, showing strong generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. Although VLM features can identify which entities are relevant to action prediction, precise manipulation also requires understanding where task-relevant entities are located within the spatial layout, how their geometric structure constrains physical interaction, and when spatial or geometric information should make a greater contribution to action prediction. To this end, we introduce {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA to organize VLA perception and action prediction around which, where, how, and when. Specifically, {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA retains VLM-based semantic entity perception which and further introduces spatial distance perception where and geometric structure perception how with adaptive spatial-geometric guidance when to enrich the perceptual information available for action prediction. Experiments across real-world settings and simulation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA.
quick_summaries.reason: 在 VLM 语义实体感知（Which）之外系统整合空间距离感知（Where）、几何结构约束（How）与自适应空间-几何门控权重（When），在多个仿真基准与真机任务验证有效性。

quick_summaries.title_en: ConsisX: Cross-View Consistency Thinking in 3D for Vision-Language-Action Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: ConsisX：面向 VLA 模型的 3D 跨视角一致性思考
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate visual perception and language understanding from vision-language models (VLMs) with action prediction for robotic manipulation. Although multi-view observations provide complementary scene information, VLMs model cross-view interactions based on 2D feature similarity, which can lead to physical inconsistency in the form of cross-view incorrect association between distinct entities and cross-view information fragmentation about the same entity. To address these challenges, we propose ConsisX, a novel VLA framework that integrates cross-view association and entity coherence to enable cross-view consistency thinking in 3D for physically consistent robotic manipulation. Specifically, Cross-View Association Modeling (CAM) is proposed to introduce cross-view spatial proximity constraints in a shared 3D space to reduce cross-view incorrect association. Entity Coherence Organization (ECO) is designed to organize cross-view local information into coherent 3D entity evidence, thereby addressing cross-view information fragmentation. quick_summaries.title_en: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: HIVE-Bench：面向第一视角双臂机器人操作的 Patch 级视觉表征评测
quick_summaries.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.
quick_summaries.subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
quick_summaries.reason: 用统一流匹配策略评测 7 大流派 20 个视觉编码器在 24 项双臂任务的表现，证实保留 Patch Token 与微调适应极其重要，且逆动力学运动读出是最强预训练评估指标（优于深度/语义/对应度）。

quick_summaries.title_en: What Should World Models Plan Over? Learning Geometry-Aligned Representations of Body Motion
quick_summaries.title_zh: MotionPort：世界模型应该在什么空间上规划？学习几何对齐的躯体运动表征
quick_summaries.abstract: We introduce MotionPort, which learns low-dimensional latent representations of body motion for accurate dynamics prediction and effective long-horizon planning. Existing world-model planners often search over action representations learned for prediction, yet we show that predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that optimization can discover successful trajectories. MotionPort addresses this mismatch by representing body trajectories rather than action chunks and organizing the search space by motion similarity, helping predicted improvements translate into successful execution. Without fine-tuning state encoders, MotionPort raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings in four domains. On the evaluated AntMaze-OGBench tasks, it achieves 72% success, compared with 4% for the strongest baseline.
quick_summaries.reason: 将世界模型规划空间从预测用动作块转为按运动相似性组织的低维躯体轨迹潜空间，在冻结编码器下将跨 3 个骨干 4 个领域的平均目标到达率从 37.9% 提至 87.8%（AntMaze 72% vs 4%）。

quick_summaries.title_en: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
quick_summaries.title_zh: 何时更好的视觉世界模型能做出更好的规划？潜空间规划的决策对齐选择（DAS）
quick_summaries.abstract: Visual world models enable goal-conditioned planning by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions in latent space. However, planning depends on how well a model ranks candidates, whereas training optimizes how accurately it predicts each one. We identify the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the part of the cost error that can reorder candidates, and show that the more training reduces the DRR, the more it improves selection (Spearman $\rho = 0.82$, vs. $0.61$ for prediction error). Building on this insight, we introduce Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in selection rule that scores candidates by the standardized consensus of several independently trained checkpoints, which averages out their checkpoint-specific residuals. Across two model families (LeWorldModel and DINO-WM) and five tasks, DAS selects better actions than single checkpoints in 12 of 18 configurations and outperforms training one model three times longer in 14 of 18. In closed loop, DAS improves success over single checkpoints in 6 of 9 pre-registered LeWM comparisons.

quick_summaries.reason: 识别决定候选重排的决策相关残差 DRR（与选优相关性 $\rho=0.82$ vs 预测误差 $0.61$），提出聚合多独立检查点标准化共识的即插即用准则 DAS，在 LeWM 与 DINO-WM 上 14/18 配置胜过三倍训练时长。

quick_summaries.title_en: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
quick_summaries.title_zh: ScaleEvals：通过免重置自主交互规模化评测通用机器人策略
quick_summaries.abstract: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. quick_summaries.title_en: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters
quick_summaries.title_zh: InteR-VLA：面向带安全滤波器部署的多样化示教抗干预 VLA
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential for learning complex robotic behaviors from demonstrations. However, learning safe behavior directly from data requires extensive coverage of safety-critical situations, which is often impractical in real-world settings. Test-time safety filters provide an alternative by correcting unsafe actions during deployment, but these interventions can drive the robot into states poorly covered by the training data, thereby degrading task performance. We introduce InteR-VLA, an intervention-robust framework for VLAs that leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden task-relevant state coverage and maintain competence under safety interventions. By better aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment under the same data budget, our approach mitigates intervention-induced distribution shift while preserving task performance. Real-world experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show that InteR-VLA maintains safety, increases Safe Success Rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal policies, and consistently outperforms nominal-data training on both evaluated VLAs.
quick_summaries.subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG); Systems and Control (eess.SY)

quick_summaries.title_en: JEPA-Shield: Safe Diffusion Planning with Latent World Models via Conformal Shielding
quick_summaries.title_zh: JEPA-Shield：基于共形安全盾的潜空间世界模型安全扩散规划
quick_summaries.abstract: Latent world models enable planning from images, but their predictions do not directly establish whether a robot will satisfy physical constraints. Two downstream models predict relative motion from imagined latent rollouts and decode unsafe geometry from the current image. quick_summaries.title_en: Fast World Planner: Advantage-Aware Action-Chunk Policy for Online Planning
quick_summaries.title_zh: SWAN：基于多模态 MPPI 与优势引导提议优化的快速世界规划器
quick_summaries.abstract: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is central to online planning for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), but its iterative refinement incurs planning latency. Reducing refinement iterations often degrades performance, motivating stronger policy guidance learned from the planner. However, existing methods typically learn from the planner through action-level alignment, which does not directly capture the complete $H$-step planner proposal. To address these limitations, we propose FaSt World PlANner (SWAN), an advantage-aware MPPI-based MBRL framework that explicitly represents and improves the complete $H$-step planner proposal to improve policy guidance for efficient online planning. For proposal representation, SWAN combines k-MPPI, a multimodal MPPI extension, with a mixture of factor analyzers (MFA) action-chunk policy to capture multiple modes and correlations across time and action dimensions. For proposal optimization, we introduce Advantage-Guided Proposal Optimization (APO), which reuses MPPI evaluations to construct an improved target using advantage estimates and trains the policy toward this target while preserving planner alignment. quick_summaries.title_en: Neural Fidelity Calibration: Turning Field Anomalies into Simulation Fine-Tuning
quick_summaries.title_zh: 神经保真度校准：将外场异常转化为仿真微调（NFC）
quick_summaries.abstract: A policy that transfers from simulation to a lab robot often fails in the field. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), a framework based on conditional flow matching that infers online, directly from a robot's execution data, both simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity - the remaining dynamics discrepancy and the gap between perceived and true environment geometry. A simulation-trained anomaly detector determines when recalibration or fine-tuning is required using onboard sensory signals alone, while an exploration policy actively modulates posterior uncertainty using optimism in the face of uncertainty. Across five robot platforms with up to 39 calibrated parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain map, NFC achieves the most accurate posterior distributions compared to established simulation-based inference baselines. In physical outdoor experiments with a wheeled robot suffering an axle failure across snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC increases rough-terrain navigation success from 26% to 70% while reducing orientation jerk by 88%.

quick_summaries.title_en: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation
quick_summaries.title_zh: 面向信息增益 Sim-to-Real 适应的神经保真度校准
quick_summaries.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) can transfer agile robot skills from simulation to the real world, but closing the sim-to-real gap by domain randomization requires expert physics knowledge, and simulator calibration from real data typically targets a few hand-picked parameters. The framework is informative: the pretrained policy is fine-tuned only when an anomaly is detected, sequential NFC seeds its proposal from the simulation-pretrained estimator, and a hallucination policy modulates posterior uncertainty following optimism in the face of uncertainty. NFC attains the most accurate posteriors among established simulation-based inference methods on five robots with up to 39 physical parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain. quick_summaries.title_en: Learning a Food World Model That Predicts the Next State from Production Data
quick_summaries.title_zh: 从产线数据学习预测下一状态的食品抓取世界模型

quick_summaries.title_en: Defending Vision-Language-Action Models against Transferable Attacks via Visual-Proprioceptive Consistency
quick_summaries.title_zh: 基于视觉-本体感觉一致性防御 VLA 模型的可迁移对抗攻击
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in a wide range of robotic tasks. However, adversarial attacks in VLA models have shown strong transferability across robotic tasks, posing significant threats to robotic systems. Despite their different attack strategies, we observe that these transferable attacks share a common consequence: they disrupt the VLA model's perception towards the robot itself. Motivated by this observation, we propose a proprioception-grounded defense framework that leverages trusted proprioceptive information to detect and mitigate transferable adversarial attacks. Specifically, we utilize the robot's proprioceptive states to establish a trusted spatial reference, and compare it with the robot's perceived location inferred from visual features. Discrepancies between these two sources provide a reliable signal for detecting adversarial attacks. Extensive experiments demonstrate effective detection of transferable adversarial patches and improved closed-loop performance. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our defense on real-world robotic tasks.

quick_summaries.reason: 利用可信本体感觉建立空间参考并与视觉特征推断的机械臂位置比对，检测并缓解跨任务可迁移对抗补丁对闭环 VLA 控制的破坏，完成真机验证。

quick_summaries.title_en: Knowing What You Carry: Scalable Physics-Anchored World Models for Robotic Planning with Liquid Payloads
quick_summaries.title_zh: 知你所载：面向液体负载机器人规划的可扩展物理锚定世界模型

It provides training data and a high-fidelity reference. quick_summaries.title_en: AlpaSafe: Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
quick_summaries.title_zh: AlpaSafe：面向自动驾驶 VLA 模型的风险感知候选轨迹选择
quick_summaries.abstract: Reasoning-based driving vision-language-action (VLA) models propose multiple candidate trajectories at each decision, yet only one is executed. Standard evaluation scores the best candidate, assuming an oracle selector that deployment lacks, and leaves the risk of the executed candidate unexamined. Existing online evaluators typically close this gap with a purpose-trained scene or world model, often rolling out each candidate through it at inference time. We introduce AlpaSafe, a risk-aware trajectory selector that reuses the scene representation a frozen driving VLA computes while proposing its candidates. AlpaSafe reads the last hidden token of the VLA's prompt prefill. A lightweight head, trained on the closed-loop simulation outcomes of the candidates, fuses this token with each candidate trajectory and predicts a relative score and collision/offroad logits. A fixed rule removes candidates dominated on the two risk logits and selects the highest-scoring candidate among those remaining, adding neither rollouts nor VLA training. Experiments on 525 AlpaSim scenes show that AlpaSafe outperforms Alpamayo's default first-sample rule and uniform random selection in selected regret and top-1 agreement, and reduces the collision-at-fault or offroad rate from 6.41% and 6.10% to 4.93%. The selector has 1.7M parameters and takes 0.75 ms per decision.
quick_summaries.subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
quick_summaries.reason: 直接复用冻结自动驾驶 VLA 预填充末位隐状态并接入仅 1.7M 参数的轻量评分头（0.75 ms），免重训练或世界模型推演即将 AlpaSim 碰撞/冲出道路率从 6.41%/6.10% 降至 4.93%。

quick_summaries.title_en: IRIS: Inverse Dynamics from Random Exploration with Eye-in-hand Sensing
quick_summaries.title_zh: IRIS：结合随机探索预训练与眼在手传感的逆动力学视频操作
quick_summaries.abstract: Imagine-then-execute methods offer a promising paradigm for video-based manipulation, where a video planner predicts future visual subgoals and an inverse dynamics model (IDM) grounds them into robot actions. Despite their promise, these methods remain limited by action grounding. First, the IDM is typically trained on limited task-specific demonstrations and can generalize poorly even when given oracle visual subgoals, indicating that action grounding remains a bottleneck beyond visual planning errors. Second, precise execution benefits from eye-in-hand observations, but eye-in-hand video planning is both hard to learn and hard to scale: the viewpoint moves with the robot, and such videos are scarce at internet scale. To overcome these challenges, we propose IRIS, a video-based manipulation framework that learns a highly generalizable, execution-aware IDM. First, IRIS scales action grounding by pretraining the IDM on task-agnostic random exploration data, which provides diverse visual state transitions paired with robot actions without human task annotation. Second, it extends the IDM with eye-in-hand sensing through a two-stage training scheme, without requiring eye-in-hand video planning. quick_summaries.reason: 在无任务标注的随机探索数据上预训练可泛化逆动力学模型（IDM），再经两阶段融合眼在手视角执行视频规划器生成的高层视觉子目标，避免学习稀缺的眼在手视频生成。

quick_summaries.title_en: LIBERO-MOR: A Multimodal Robustness Benchmark Across the Vision-Language-Action Pipeline
quick_summaries.title_zh: LIBERO-MOR：覆盖 VLA 全链路的多模态鲁棒性评测基准
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance on robot manipulation benchmarks. Translating this progress into reliable deployment calls for systematic evaluation of how policies respond to variations throughout the robot interaction loop. We introduce LIBERO-MOR, a multimodal robustness benchmark across the vision-language-action pipeline. Built on standard LIBERO, it covers five deployment-facing domains: vision, language, proprioception, action execution, and environment. The benchmark comprises 22 deployment-inspired perturbations, each evaluated at three severity levels across 40 tasks under a paired clean-perturbed protocol, enabling controlled and reproducible comparisons. We evaluate seven representative VLA models spanning diverse action-generation mechanisms. Our experiments reveal substantial robustness gaps behind high clean-task success, together with shared vulnerabilities and distinct model-specific failure patterns across domains. Severity analysis further distinguishes progressive degradation, collapse at stronger interventions, and failures triggered at the mildest tested level. By connecting aggregate performance to pipeline domains, individual perturbations, and intervention strength, LIBERO-MOR provides a systematic framework for diagnosing VLA robustness and guiding the development of more reliable robot policies.
quick_summaries.reason: 在 LIBERO 上围绕视觉、语言、本体、执行与环境五大维度构建 22 种三级强度扰动，系统诊断 7 个代表性 VLA 模型在高干净成功率背后的多模态脆弱模式。

quick_summaries.title_en: ViewPACT: Multi-View Geometric Augmentation and Pose-Action Co-Training for Viewpoint-Robust Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: ViewPACT：面向视角鲁棒操作的多视角几何增强与位姿-动作协同训练
quick_summaries.abstract: Image policies are scalable but remain brittle to camera viewpoint changes. On LIBERO, we identify proprioception as an input shortcut: masking robot states sharply degrades several policies, while retraining from images alone recovers much of the loss. We introduce ViewPACT, an image policy trained with privileged geometric supervision. Auxiliary objectives recover end-effector and task-relevant object poses in the camera frame, while deployment requires only RGB observations. Joint geometric supervision improves mean simulation success from 37.4% to 78.4% under unseen external-camera viewpoints, with more modest gains under separately evaluated object, scene, and camera-intrinsic shifts. Across four real-robot tasks, combining simulated and real-image geometric supervision achieves 68.1% mean success, versus 3.1% for fixed-view behavior cloning and 30.6% for the strongest evaluated alternative. These results support geometric supervision for viewpoint robustness in the evaluated fixed-view demonstration setting.
quick_summaries.reason: 揭示 LIBERO 中本体感觉会成为视角泛化捷径，通过训练期相机系末端与目标物体位姿辅助监督（部署仅需单 RGB），将未见外部相机视角下成功率从 37.4% 提至 78.4%（真机 68.1%）。

quick_summaries.title_en: Your Diffusion-Based Driving Planner Only Needs a Nudge
quick_summaries.title_zh: PlanNudge：冻结扩散驾驶规划器的轻量离线 RL 微调补丁
quick_summaries.abstract: Diffusion-based planners capture the multimodality of human driving behavior well, yet covariate shift in closed-loop driving can lead them to generate trajectories that result in collisions or road departures. Reinforcement learning (RL) finetuning offers a promising way to tackle this issue, but applying it to diffusion-based planners is complicated by their iterative denoising process and receding-horizon execution. We find that small adjustments to the planned trajectories can prevent many of these unsafe outcomes. Motivated by this observation, we propose PlanNudge, which preserves the learned planning capabilities of a pretrained diffusion-based planner by freezing it and trains a lightweight policy that we call the nudge policy. At each planning step, the nudge policy outputs a nudge, a two-dimensional adjustment of the speed and curvature of the plan from the frozen planner. The nudge policy is a multilayer perceptron that predicts the nudge in a single forward pass, and both dimensions directly change the motion of the vehicle, so standard off-policy RL can train it in closed-loop simulation. We evaluate PlanNudge on nuPlan, a large-scale autonomous driving benchmark based on real-world driving data. quick_summaries.reason: 冻结预训练扩散规划器以保留多模态驾驶先验，仅用轻量单步前向 MLP 通过闭环异策略 RL 输出速度与曲率微调偏移量，在 nuPlan 上以约六分之一交互步数达到 SOTA RL 微调得分。

quick_summaries.title_en: InfoField3D: Differentiable Information Field for Embodied Task-Oriented View Planning
quick_summaries.title_zh: InfoField3D：面向具身任务导向视点规划的可微信息场
quick_summaries.abstract: Effective task execution requires embodied agents to select observation positions that provide sufficient task-relevant information. Existing approaches typically predict viewpoints with learned models or score discrete candidates, but they either struggle to incorporate new constraints such as reachability or require extensive candidate evaluation to search. We introduce InfoField3D, which lifts geometry-bound information into a differentiable analytic field, whose value at each 3D observation position represents the task-required information accessible there. It uses low-order spherical harmonics to encode directional information responses and analytic line integrals of Gaussian occupancy functions to model occlusion along lines of sight. This formulation casts task-driven camera placement as a well-studied constrained continuous optimization problem, enabling both flexible incorporation of constraints through the feasible domain and efficient viewpoint search even in the presence of occlusion. Experiments show that InfoField3D compactly preserves the pointwise information landscape with high fidelity and generally recommends higher-quality, more robust viewpoints at lower search cost than the evaluated baselines. quick_summaries.title_en: Self-Refining VLA Sampling
quick_summaries.title_zh: 面向上下文流式 VLA 的推理期自精炼采样（P&P）
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models typically use flow-based generative modeling to learn a rich, often multimodal, distribution of robot actions. Generating samples from flow-based methods involves iteratively updating random noise, and distinct noise samples from the same state can result in distinct trajectories and task outcomes. Existing test-time scaling methods improve action chunk generation via selection, aggregation, or correction, but commonly require the generation of large ensembles of candidates or the training of an external corrector. We adapt Predict-and-Perturb (P&P), a self-refinement procedure for flow-based models originally used for mode-seeking in video generation, to the robotics domain. We find that applying P&P to VLA models requires modifications to the refinement process used in video generation due to differences in the underlying structure of the data. Across 400 episodes of LIBERO evaluated using SmolVLA, P&P improves upon the stock baseline by 5.3 percentage points. Further, episode-level P\&P uncertainty correlates strongly with task failure (AUC 0.851).
quick_summaries.comments: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Learn@Deploy Workshop
quick_summaries.reason: 将视频生成的 Predict-and-Perturb 自精炼机制适配到机器人流式动作块采样，免外接打分器在 400 轮 LIBERO 上将 SmolVLA 提升 5.3 个百分点且单集不确定性与失败率高度相关（AUC 0.851）。

quick_summaries.title_en: Reset Dependence Is Embodied: Training Protocol Changes Which Morphologies Appear Optimal
quick_summaries.title_zh: 重置规则具有具身依赖性：训练协议改变机器人形态协同设计的最优排序
quick_summaries.abstract: Robot co-design benchmarks rank bodies after training their controllers under a fixed episode protocol, but that protocol can change the ranking itself. Consequently, two studies can select different bodies from the same corpus even when they use the same task and evaluator. We study one part of that protocol, the reset rule, which ends a training episode when the robot's torso falls below a height threshold. We train proximal policy optimization (PPO) controllers for 100 DERL-evolved UNIMAL bodies with this threshold at 20% of each body's starting torso height (Standard), at 50% (Strict), or with no threshold (Reset-free), and score every controller with the same evaluator. The threshold changes which bodies look best: the rankings after Strict and Reset-free training correlate at only 0.21, against about 0.89 if seed noise were the only difference. Removing fall resets costs some bodies far more than others. Bodies evolved on flat ground lose 45% of their per-step reward relative to Standard training, and those evolved on variable terrain only 16%. Permutation tests over bodies support this difference, and on 24 bodies, flat-ground bodies gain the most from Strict over Reset-free training under both PPO and soft actor-critic (SAC). quick_summaries.title_en: Action Windows Are Inherently Temporal: A Benchmark for Time-Sensitive Robotic Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: AWAIT：面向时间敏感型机器人操作的动作窗口基准
quick_summaries.abstract: Vision-language model (VLM) agents have surpassed learned-policy baselines on existing robotic manipulation benchmarks. However, these agents still struggle with time-sensitive everyday tasks that existing benchmarks for VLM agents cover only partially. In these tasks, evolving physical processes create finite windows for successful intervention. These action windows are inherently temporal and impose a shared time budget on decision making and physical execution. Coordinating intervention within this budget requires agents to determine when the window opens. We introduce AWAIT, a simulation benchmark that evaluates task completion within action windows while accounting for decision and execution time. Our evaluation reveals difficulties in recognizing window onset and shows that successive decisions and movements can exhaust an action window even when each decision takes less than the window duration. Project page: this https URL .
quick_summaries.subjects: Robotics (cs.RO) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

quick_summaries.title_en: TASC: Time-to-Collision Anticipation and Selective Crowd Attention for Non-Holonomic Service Robots
quick_summaries.title_zh: TASC：面向非完整约束服务机器人的碰撞时间预判与人群选择性注意 RL 导航
quick_summaries.abstract: Service robots that share corridors and lobbies with people must keep moving without endangering them. Reactive planners can stop indefinitely in dense crowds (the freezing robot problem), whereas the attention-based learned navigators that dominate the standard crowd benchmark assume holonomic motion or emit discrete actions unsuited to a differential-drive base. This paper presents TASC, a navigation system for a non-holonomic service robot that integrates an attention-based crowd encoder, an anticipatory collision feature, and a continuous-control policy. We adapt the dual-selection attention module, originally developed for discrete-action value learning, to proximal policy optimization for continuous velocity control, and add a closing-speed time-to-collision feature, a conservative estimate of the time to contact that serves as both an observation and a reward term. The policy is trained on a high-fidelity 3D robot model in NVIDIA Isaac Lab with 10,000 parallel environments, social-force-model pedestrians, and randomized crowd sizes. In 30,000 evaluation episodes, each run to its end, the policy timed out in fewer than 0.5% at every tested crowd density. This liveness comes at a cost: pedestrian collisions rise from 4.5% with five pedestrians to 17.4% with ten. quick_summaries.title_en: Grounded in Contact: Reducing Floating and Interpenetration Artifacts with Multimodal Skill-Effect Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: 以多模态技能效应世界模型减少接触操作中的悬空与穿模伪影
quick_summaries.abstract: Learning to predict the effects of contact-rich manipulation skills requires models that represent distinct outcome modes rather than a single expected result. Even for basic skills such as pushing, picking, and placing, small variations in contact conditions or object geometry can produce qualitatively different object motions under nearly identical states and actions. Deterministic and Gaussian models tend to average over these alternatives or represent them as a single broad distribution, obscuring distinct modes such as sliding, toppling, and rotating. We study probabilistic skill-effect models that learn multimodal distributions over object pose changes given partial point clouds and actions. We instantiate this abstraction with three representative model classes: mixture density networks, state tokenization, and flow matching, each paired with latent dynamics for next-step prediction. Across diverse objects and skills, explicitly multimodal models predict which outcome occurs more accurately than deterministic and Gaussian baselines. In planning, flow matching significantly improves task success over the deterministic baseline on every skill and achieves the highest success on every multi-step sequence. quick_summaries.title_en: CarlHOI: Counterfactual Predictive Imagination for Generalizable Multi-Humanoid Object Interaction under Constrained Environments
quick_summaries.title_zh: CarlHOI：面向受限环境多人形协同搬运的反事实预测想象
quick_summaries.abstract: Recent advances in physics-based humanoid control enable teams of varying sizes to coordinate their movements and cooperatively transport shared objects. However, adapting learned cooperative behaviors to unseen environmental constraints remains challenging, particularly when obstacles require coordinated detours and changes in team configuration. We propose CarlHOI, a counterfactual predictive imagination framework built upon a counterfactual-anchored relational latent world model (CarlWM) for human-object interaction (HOI), enabling multi-humanoid teams to adapt to unseen environmental constraints without retraining their underlying cooperative control policies. CarlHOI explicitly represents the shared object, individual humanoids, and environmental obstacles as interacting entities. Trained offline using counterfactual simulator rollouts, the model imagines alternative collective futures under different shared waypoint commands, predicting how the coupled humanoid team and object would respond. By evaluating these imagined outcomes through predicted progress, failure, and contact risks, and long-horizon value estimates, CarlHOI selects adaptive guidance commands while preserving the pretrained cooperative controller. quick_summaries.title_en: How Should a Home Robot Update Its Memories When Human Routines Change?
quick_summaries.title_zh: 当人类日常作息变化时，家庭机器人应如何更新记忆？
quick_summaries.abstract: A home robot that helps with chores needs to know where objects are, but people move objects according to routines that change and later change back. The robot's memory must adapt to the new routine without erasing experience that may become useful again. One approach is to have a language model maintain written summaries of the home from the robot's own observations, but existing evaluations of such memories use static worlds. We explore simulated households where a resident gets sick, recovers, and later gets sick again. We compare a rule that keeps every room an object has been seen in, language-model memories that store only written summaries, and language-model memories that can also read the raw history of sightings. The rule outperforms every summary-only memory, and giving language models the sighting history closes the gap. Surprisingly, writing summaries on top of the history adds nothing we can measure. When the illness returns, methods that keep the history search better than they did the first time, while summary-only methods show no consistent improvement. Deleting the first illness from memory removes all of the rule's gain and part of theirs. The summaries recorded where objects went during the illness but rarely distinguished sick-day patterns from normal routines. quick_summaries.title_en: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
quick_summaries.title_zh: Motion Mamba 2.0：面向长程人形机器人控制的自回归扩散 Mamba
quick_summaries.abstract: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. quick_summaries.title_en: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
quick_summaries.title_zh: SuperNav-1.5：面向智能体导航系统的结构化空间记忆
quick_summaries.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. quick_summaries.title_en: MoMa-NMP: Scene-Scale Neural Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators
quick_summaries.title_zh: MoMa-NMP：面向移动操作机器人的场景级神经运动规划
quick_summaries.abstract: Mobile manipulators operating in homes and other complex environments must coordinate their base and arm over long horizons, navigating around obstacles, through narrow passages, and between constrained workspaces. Neural motion planners can provide fast closed-loop planning from partial observations, but scaling them to room-sized environments is difficult because generating high-quality training trajectories is itself a challenging motion-planning problem. To address this, we introduce MoMa-DemoSmith, a demonstration-generation pipeline that separates the problem into global path discovery for large complex scenes and local motion refinement for collision avoidance. This key separation enables the generation of millions of challenging whole-body trajectories across our procedurally generated scenes. We train MoMa-NMP on these demonstrations through behavior cloning (BC) followed by privileged on-policy distillation, achieving 87.0% success on our simulation benchmark and 77.5% across 80 trials in unseen real-world scenes. See video results at this https URL .
quick_summaries.reason: 将全局路径发现与局部避障精修分离以在程序化场景生成百万级全身运动规划示教，经 BC 与特权在策略蒸馏后在仿真达 87.0%、未见真实室内场景 80 轮达 77.5% 成功率。

quick_summaries.title_en: One Latent World for Heterogeneous LiDARs: A Scan Pattern Agnostic 4D World Model via Direct Ray Decoding
quick_summaries.title_zh: 面向异构激光雷达的扫描模式无关 4D 潜空间世界模型
quick_summaries.abstract: LiDAR world models generate and predict metric 3D observations in the form of LiDAR scans. They typically synthesize scans following the scan pattern of their training sensor or render them from an intermediate 3D surface or field. However, following one scan pattern limits transfer to LiDARs with other patterns, and rendering from intermediate geometry can cause incorrect depths and false returns. In this paper, we propose a scan pattern agnostic 4D LiDAR world model that decouples the scene from sensor observation, so one spatial latent can be observed by heterogeneous LiDARs at the same mounting position without regeneration. Our decoder predicts the hit probability and depth of each ray directly from the latent, combining global scene context with local features retrieved at a preliminary depth. Without an intermediate surface or field, it reduces incorrect depths and false returns, and as each ray is decoded independently from one latent, LiDARs that share a ray receive the same return and observe one consistent scene. Finally, a diffusion transformer generates scenes in this latent and predicts 4D sequences from observed latents warped by the given ego and object motion. quick_summaries.title_en: HERO: Hierarchical Region-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Exploration
quick_summaries.title_zh: HERO：面向自主探索的分层区域感知强化学习框架
quick_summaries.abstract: Autonomous exploration is widely used to map unknown environments, yet maintaining both path efficiency and low online computation remains difficult as environment scale increases. Hierarchical planners reduce global search through coarse regional representations but often rely on handcrafted local viewpoint-selection rules. quick_summaries.title_en: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation

quick_summaries.abstract: Humanoid box pushing is challenging when the physical properties of the task, such as the box mass and the ramp inclination, are unknown before the push begins. Hardware experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid show that the policy adapts its torso pitch during continuous pushing on an inclined treadmill, with box masses up to 19 kg and ramp inclinations up to 12.6 degrees. quick_summaries.title_en: Policy-intrinsic Demonstration Curation
quick_summaries.title_zh: PICKER：基于预训练策略自身错误一致性的内禀示教筛选
quick_summaries.abstract: Fine-tuning a robot policy for a new target task requires target demonstrations, but only a few are available. Demonstrations of other tasks can fill this gap, and demonstration curation selects the useful ones among these candidates. Retrieval-based curation selects the candidates that are most similar to the target demonstrations. Since it does not use the policy, any candidate that looks similar receives a high score. Performance-aware curation therefore estimates the effect of each candidate on the policy. However, this requires training on the candidates and takes a long time. We propose a third branch, policy-intrinsic curation, which uses the policy and still takes little time. It estimates this effect with forward passes of the pretrained policy and needs no training. We instantiate this branch with PICKER (Policy-Intrinsic Curation from Known Errors). It selects the candidates on which the policy makes errors that agree with those on the target demonstrations. PICKER reaches success rates comparable to those of performance-aware curation and takes about as long as retrieval-based curation. Its selection is also stable across seeds.

quick_summaries.title_en: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds
quick_summaries.title_zh: 基于障碍函数的四足机器人安全强化学习奖励塑形
quick_summaries.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has progressed from simple control tasks to complex real-world challenges with large state spaces. quick_summaries.title_en: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
quick_summaries.title_zh: LeadVLA：面向机器人领航的跟随者感知路线执行策略

quick_summaries.title_en: Trustworthy agentic lunar robotics: safety-constrained contingent planning with a foundation-model planner
quick_summaries.title_zh: AKR：面向可信智能体月球机器人的安全约束应急重规划

quick_summaries.title_en: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: Shared Environmental Understanding for Multi-Robot Navigation
quick_summaries.title_zh: SEER：基于共享潜空间世界模型的多机器人分散式导航协同（NeurIPS 2026）
quick_summaries.abstract: Multi-robot embodied systems are typically designed to collaborate by coordinating actions, sharing trajectories, or learning joint policies. quick_summaries.title_zh: MorphHOI：面向异构角色团队协同物物交互的统一分散式策略
quick_summaries.abstract: Physics-based human-object interaction (HOI) has enabled multiple characters to cooperatively transport objects, but existing cooperative controllers largely assume homogeneous embodiments and predefined interaction tasks. quick_summaries.title_en: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
quick_summaries.title_zh: RoboInF：面向机器人操作指令忠实度的细粒度评测基准

quick_summaries.title_zh: WAVE：通过仿射翘曲冻结单物体技能实现多物体数量泛化
quick_summaries.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts. First, a selection policy picks the one object the robot works on next. Second, a warping policy reads a local view of the scene around that object, whose size does not depend on N. It emits a multiplier and an offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. Third, the skill acts under this affine warp. It is shown a scene that holds a single object, while the warp steers it around the objects it is not shown and edits the actions that are sent to the robot. Both the selection and warping policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward and use the skill as a black box, so WAVE is task-general and skill-agnostic. It requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose. We also bound the number of attempts needed to place all N objects, assuming positive expected net progress per attempt, and measure this progress for each object count. quick_summaries.title_en: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
quick_summaries.title_zh: 超越域随机化：基于习得动力学模型的足式机器人真机策略适应
quick_summaries.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

quick_summaries.title_en: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
quick_summaries.title_zh: SayDo：从纯对话到闭环机器人控制的前沿大模型安全性退化基准
quick_summaries.abstract: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. Safety evaluations run in text therefore do not predict the safety behavior of the same models when used as robot controllers.

quick_summaries.title_zh: WorldLeague：横跨 VLM、VLA 与 WAM 的 60 项任务物理智能体能力基准

quick_summaries.title_en: Imagine Smarter, Drive Faster: Efficient World Modeling for Decision-Aware Autonomous Driving
quick_summaries.title_zh: FastWorld：面向决策感知自动驾驶的原生轻量高效世界模型
quick_summaries.abstract: World models hold great promise for autonomous driving planning, yet their ability to imagine the future often comes at a formidable computational cost. Efficiency efforts, such as knowledge distillation and domain-specific pre-training, often shift this burden to costly teachers or training pipelines, leaving lightweight world modeling an open challenge. We introduce FastWorld, a natively lightweight world-model framework for efficient autonomous driving planning. FastWorld reduces computation through compact scene representations, short-horizon action-conditioned prediction, and selective candidate verification and score refinement. These designs support efficient future-informed planning without teacher distillation or additional domain-specific pre-training. On NAVSIMv1, FastWorld achieves 92.2 PDMS at 132 FPS on a single 4090 GPU. It also achieves 89.4 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2 and an average L2 of 0.40 over 3 seconds at 17 FPS on nuScenes. quick_summaries.title_en: Dynamics Forcing: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Causal Video World Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: Dynamics Forcing：缓解因果视频世界模型误差累积的训练方案
quick_summaries.abstract: Causal video world models generate block by block from their own previous outputs. Small errors in early blocks are fed back as history and grow until the scene and the robot fall apart. Teacher forcing trains on clean ground-truth history, so the model never sees the history it will actually condition on, and it also finds a shortcut: copying the previous frame instead of predicting how the scene changes. We present Dynamics Forcing, a training scheme that keeps real video as the only supervision and reshapes how history is presented. History is perturbed in three ways: random noising, self-resampling by the model itself, and joint denoising, in which the most recent blocks are still partly noisy when the next block is predicted. On top of this we move history guidance and first-frame anchor guidance from inference into training, so that the model is pushed to use its history and its reference frame rather than ignore them. Dynamics Forcing needs no teacher model, no distillation, and no additional model at inference. Applied to a 5B video model with LoRA on 77 hours of manipulation video on a single GPU, it better matches unseen real continuations and reduces error accumulation.

quick_summaries.title_en: EnvTrap: Revealing the Environment-Only Attack Surface in Embodied AI via Consequence-Blind Action Execution

quick_summaries.title_en: MOVER: Planning Beyond Motion
quick_summaries.title_zh: MOVER：残差驾驶世界模型中弱运动静态风险的事件互补路由规划
quick_summaries.abstract: Residual world models forecast a driving scene through its temporal change, so feature components that stay constant over time vanish from the residual pathway. quick_summaries.title_en: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: 潜空间转移几何如何影响世界模型规划效果
quick_summaries.abstract: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. Further analysis shows that curvature generally brings predicted futures closer together, while preserving more of the differences along the goal direction. quick_summaries.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). quick_summaries.title_en: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
quick_summaries.title_zh: MoOP：面向推理型自动驾驶 VLA 的推理与动作双目标结构化剪枝

quick_summaries.title_en: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling
quick_summaries.title_zh: WorldWeave：面向 VLN 与具身追踪的跨任务潜动作世界模型
quick_summaries.abstract: Mobile embodied agents continuously alter their observations through their own motion, while external dynamics further shape future interactions. Different mobile embodied tasks therefore capture complementary patterns of state evolution, yet jointly learning world dynamics across such interactions remains less explored. We investigate this problem through Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) and Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT), which respectively involve navigation toward a stationary goal and interaction with a moving target. We propose WorldWeave, a cross-task world model that couples shared predictive dynamics with task-specific adaptation. Instead of conditioning state transitions on heterogeneous physical actions, WorldWeave learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse-forward dynamics, establishing a shared transition representation across tasks. The resulting future-state predictions are adaptively integrated into task-specific representations for downstream decision making. Experiments across multiple VLN and EVT benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over specialized baselines.

quick_summaries.title_en: AERIN: Aerial Instance Navigation with a Visual World Model
quick_summaries.title_zh: AERIN：基于紧凑目标条件视觉世界模型的无人机实例导航
quick_summaries.abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs. In such tasks, high-altitude observations provide broad ground coverage for efficient search, but targets occupy fewer pixels, making instance verification and action selection more difficult. We present AERIN, a visual world model that uses action-conditioned prediction to guide the UAV toward the target while adjusting its viewpoint to obtain higherquality observations for subsequent instance verification. Highaltitude navigation requires fine-grained target details and scene context relevant to visibility, but repeatedly predicting dense visual representations of this information is computationally expensive. AERIN addresses this challenge with a compact, fixedsize, target-conditioned latent state that separately represents both for efficient action evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that AERIN outperforms the evaluated baselines in target approach and observation quality, while requiring substantially less decision time than similar world models.

quick_summaries.title_en: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: ViTrust：面向可变形物理世界模型的 3D 观测信任度学习
quick_summaries.abstract: Learning deformable physical world models requires dynamics that generalize beyond observed motion. Accurate reconstruction alone does not ensure accurate future prediction, motivating us to learn how observations should influence physical identification. However, visual reliability alone does not determine how informative an observation is about physical dynamics. We propose ViTrust to learn 3D observation trust, determining how strongly each tracked point influences physical identification. Its key design is a visual-contact trust adapter that combines pointwise spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph to predict time-varying observation weights. A single-stage, shared-forward objective jointly optimizes these weights and physical parameters through weighted geometry and correspondence losses, with constraints to prevent observation-weight collapse. All learning uses only the observed prefix. The fitted physics remains fixed for future prediction under supplied controls. Experiments on real-world sequences demonstrate improved future prediction over the evaluated baselines, alongside qualitative demonstrations of novel-control rollouts and cross-object transfer.

quick_summaries.title_en: SilentWAM: Planning in the Masked State of a Diffusion World Model
quick_summaries.title_zh: SilentWAM：免视频解码的扩散世界模型掩码隐态直接规划

Learned planning queries attend to these masked positions and the observed context, and a continuous head predicts the trajectory in the same forward pass. With a single front camera, \method reaches 92.0 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 89.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, with an end-to-end latency of 60.3\,ms.

quick_summaries.title_zh: ClothCast：部分可观测条件下基于点云刚体先验的生成式衣物世界模型

quick_summaries.title_en: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: 迈向对抗鲁棒的潜空间动力学世界模型
quick_summaries.abstract: Latent dynamic world models have proven to be highly versatile tools for embodied artificial intelligence systems, enabling online action planning, safe policy evaluation, and scalable policy learning. However, this versatility makes world models a vulnerable and centralized point of failure as a compromised model can impact planning, evaluation, and training at once. Therefore it is critical that the security and robustness properties of world models are properly understood before they are universally deployed in embodied AI systems. In this work we take a unifying approach towards this understanding, developing two novel attacks against world models, named state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks, aimed directly at impacting downstream systems, and proposing a new theoretical lens through which to study the robustness of latent dynamic world models. Through our analysis we identify robust latent space encoders as the key component of robust world models. We empirically validate this finding on four separate latent dynamic world model families, studying Dino World Model, Le World Model, r2Dreamer, and Cosmos 3, demonstrating significant improvements in robustness through adversarial encoder model training.

quick_summaries.title_en: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models
quick_summaries.title_zh: RLB：基于反事实世界模型基准线的低方差策略梯度强化学习
quick_summaries.abstract: Agents in complex, stochastic environments must contend with dynamics that can exceed their world models' predictive capacity and randomness that obscure the consequences of their actions. We hypothesize that, compared to imagining entirely new trajectories in such complex environments, it can be easier to transform observed trajectories with alternative actions. Counterfactual world models condition on observations to predict alternative outcomes under the same underlying environmental randomness, using experience as a reference for predicting action-dependent changes. We present a policy gradient estimator, REINFORCE Look Back (RLB), that uses counterfactual returns as baselines to distinguish action effects from environmental luck, and prove conditions for unbiasedness and variance reduction. In settings where environmental evolution is harder to predict than action-induced changes, we show that counterfactual world models are easier to learn and support better policy learning than ordinary world models. Our findings suggest that counterfactual thinking can help agents learn effective behavior without independently reproducing the full complexity of their worlds.

quick_summaries.abstract: An embodied agent built on a language model goes to work with the weights it was given and keeps them for life.
